description:
FILES: dispatcher.ex, wherever load_all/1 is called in the session runner.

Replace the per-dispatch scan of Extension.t() handler maps with a :bag ETS table lookup.

TABLE SPEC:
- Type: :bag (multiple rows per key)
- Row format: {event_type :: atom(), ext_id :: String.t(), handler_fn :: function()}
- Options: {:read_concurrency, true}, :protected
- Name: session-scoped (NOT a named global table -- multiple sessions must coexist)

POPULATION: After all extensions are loaded (post load_all/1 or equivalent), iterate extensions and insert one row per handler. Table is populated once and read many times.

OWNERSHIP: The ETS table must be owned by a long-lived process that outlives individual dispatch calls. Options: (a) the session supervisor process owns it, (b) a dedicated TableOwner GenServer under the session supervisor. Do NOT create it in a process that may exit before the session ends. Document which approach is chosen.

DISPATCHER CHANGE: Dispatcher.all_handlers/2 currently takes [Extension.t()] and scans. Change signature to accept either the ETS table reference or a context that carries it. The table reference must reach the Dispatcher on every emit call. Evaluate whether to thread it through Context.t() (add a handlers_table field) or pass as explicit argument to emit/3.

Extension.t() structs are still built identically -- ETS is populated FROM them, not instead of them. Introspection functions (get_all_tools, get_all_commands, etc.) continue to work off the in-memory Extension.t() list.

TEST: Update dispatcher_test.exs and extensions_runner_test.exs. Tests that currently pass [Extension.t()] to Dispatcher.emit must be updated to populate and pass a table reference instead.
title: ETS handler dispatch table
